claims.text: Standard additively manufactured MoNbTaW has a predominantly single-phase BCC microstructure.
Standard additively manufactured MoNbTaW exhibits high yield strength but limited ductility.
Powder-bed fusion at 300–350 W and approximately 800 mm/s constitutes an optimized processing window for MoNbTaW.
Combining the proposed laser parameters with real-time thermal monitoring will actively control solidification.
The proposed processing and monitoring intervention will promote reproducible formation of a dual-phase microstructure in MoNbTaW.
The resulting microstructure will be bimodal, with a dominant hard BCC phase and a secondary softer phase.
The secondary phase may be B2 or a segregated ductile phase located at grain boundaries or within grains.
Coexistence of the two phases will create internal strain fields and composite-like interfaces.
The internal strain fields and interfaces will enhance dislocation storage.
The dual-phase interfaces will impede crack propagation.
The hard BCC phase will provide high strength.
The softer secondary phase will facilitate plastic deformation.
The optimized MoNbTaW samples will have higher yield strength than standard AM-processed MoNbTaW.
The optimized MoNbTaW samples will have greater ductility than standard AM-processed MoNbTaW.
Simultaneous strength and ductility improvement depends on maintaining a precise thermal-processing window that consistently produces the dual-phase microstructure.
Deviations from the proposed thermal-processing window may produce inhomogeneous microstructures and eliminate the expected improvements.
